claims.text: The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating has a relatively coarse grain structure.
A controlled annealing treatment can refine the near-surface grain structure of the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
High-temperature sliding of the refined FeNiCrCoCu coating will promote dynamic amorphization and formation of an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer.
The ultra-nanocrystalline surface layer operates in the inverse Hall-Petch regime.
Formation of the ultra-nanocrystalline layer shifts deformation from dislocation-mediated bulk flow to grain-boundary sliding.
Grain-boundary-mediated deformation in the transformed layer reduces friction and wear.
The annealed and refined FeNiCrCoCu coating will have a lower wear rate than the untreated coating.
The annealed and refined FeNiCrCoCu coating will have a lower friction coefficient than the untreated coating.
The annealed coating will exhibit an ultra-nanocrystalline, amorphized surface layer detectable by TEM or STEM.
The untreated, coarser FeNiCrCoCu coating does not preferentially form an ultra-nanocrystalline surface layer during high-temperature sliding.
The predicted transformation and tribological benefits are restricted to high-temperature sliding conditions.
Room-temperature static or sliding tests may not produce the same dynamic amorphization or inverse Hall-Petch behavior.
Inverse Hall-Petch behavior has been documented in CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy.
Dynamic amorphization associated with an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer has been documented in CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy.
